title: OpsTruss run record
description: record.json of a run in .opstruss/runs/<stack>/<run>/: who ran what and when, and how it ended. Readers ignore fields they do not know.

opstruss.description: The version of the OpsTruss that ran it, as opstruss version prints it; for people and tools that read old runs, never a reason to refuse one.

trigger.description: What made the run, as event.trigger says: cli, schedule, every, and later others.

simulated.description: For a run of the command line with --event, or of runs rerun: the trigger whose event its caller wrote or ran again, which event.trigger says inside the run.

reason.description: Why a run ended cancelled: requested (opstruss runs cancel), concurrency (a call with concurrency: cancel), or interrupted (its process died).

tasks.description: The tasks of the project that ran inside the run, through task:, needs, or a unit, by name, with one outcome for all their calls.

events_incomplete.description: events.jsonl lacks events that could not be written, as on a full disk.

rerun_of.description: The run that opstruss runs rerun ran again.

replay.description: Of a run of a task, up, or destroy: what opstruss runs rerun needs beside the record. Without it, the run cannot run again.

trigger.description: The key of the trigger whose event made the run, in the project file.

payload.description: sealed: the inputs and the event are in the replay file beside the record, encrypted with the data key of the stack; unavailable: they were not kept, as error says. Absent when the run needs neither.
